answer: The violet detector writes to basalt, and timber reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 131 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 280 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 20 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
